g.text: Cross-layer coupling is real but local

text.style: font-size: 23.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: How do parameters inside one component interact?

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: Each bar is a co-location statistic against a null that preserves every marginal and destroys only the pairing, so they are comparable.

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: A component binds a computational UNIT almost perfectly — in SwiGLU, gate row i, up row i and down column i are one neuron, and components own

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: them together at 138× chance (89× above a layer-shifted control). Binding then decays: loosely within a head, barely across adjacent layers,

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: and at exactly chance for the composed head pairs that make a virtual attention head.
